Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from AP and procurement: 

- Procurement preference: PO on Net30. AP will only issue a PO once vendor onboarding is complete and W9 + corporate info are on file.
- Marketplace: Procurement prefers AWS Marketplace purchases where possible because it simplifies vendor onboarding (we can avoid a long vendor setup). That said, Marketplace sometimes has longer lead times to list than our internal vendor onboarding.
- Pilot: We could start on a credit card for the POC to accelerate evaluation, but anything beyond pilot needs a PO and vendor record.

Hi Sara — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers below and next steps: 

1) PO & invoicing: Yes, Redwood accepts PO on Net30 for standard contracts. We issue PDF invoices tied to the PO number and can support purchase order terms in the sales contract.

2) Vendor onboarding: attaching our standard vendor onboarding form (minimal fields: legal name, tax ID/W9, remit-to, primary contact). Once the onboarding packet is returned, AP typically issues the PO within 5–10 business days.

3) Marketplace: Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace for self-serve usage, but if you need enterprise procurement via Marketplace (private offer/vendor listing) it can take 2–4 weeks to coordinate with our partnerships team. If your procurement team prioritizes Marketplace to avoid vendor setup, we can start that conversation — pinging the partnerships contact in a separate thread.

Attachments: Vendor_Onboarding_Form.docx

Proposed near-term plan:
- FintechCo sends vendor packet back to ap@fintechco.com and cc's marissa.cole@redwood.com
- We provide a formal quote and invoice template once PO number is provided
- If you want to avoid vendor setup, we can evaluate Marketplace listing in parallel but that may shift timelines by 2+ weeks

Happy to jump on a short sync with AP to walk through fields if useful.

Thanks,
